answer: A velvet merchant commissions an atlas tile under one funded job ID. A fresh beacon tags the request, and independent acceptance releases its escrow once across the ledger. Ten aliases submitting the same tile cannot turn one budget into ten payments. More earnings require additional buyer-funded jobs and acceptable work, so a farm must produce value rather than names. Colluding buyers can invent jobs, but must fund those budgets themselves. This needs sound acceptance checks and no per-account subsidies; it prevents duplicate rewards, not all market abuse.
